description: A throwaway webhook-triggered workflow whose only real node throws deliberately, wired to WF9 as its errorWorkflow, proving the error handler actually fires.
why_it_exists: An error handler that is configured but never fires is worse than none, because it creates the belief that failures are being reported. This is the live proof that a thrown error in a workflow with settings.errorWorkflow set reaches WF9.

expect.error_message: QA Error Handler Test — deliberate controlled failure — safe to ignore. This is a controlled test of WF9 error handling.

assertions: The failing workflow declares settings.errorWorkflow = JfaCOxRq0FjZ5JWb; without that setting the throw is invisible to WF9.
The error message identifies itself as a deliberate test in its own text, so an owner who receives the alert is not misled into investigating a real fault.
The webhook responds immediately (onReceived) and the failure happens after the response, so the caller sees success while the error path still runs.
This workflow's webhook path is a live unauthenticated GET endpoint on the n8n host; anyone who has the path can fire a synthetic error alert at the owner.
target_unresolved_reason: kind is "integration": not executed by harness/run.js.
